one_liner: C11 DSP library (FFT, DCT/DST, DWT, CWT, STFT) with IR interpreter plus runtime gcc JIT; beats KissFFT only at some sizes.
what_it_does: A static C library that builds transforms from one faf_config struct (faf_create_fft, faf_create_rfft, DCT/DST I-IV, MDCT, STFT, five DWT families, CWT/CQT) and runs them with faf_execute on caller-owned buffer descriptors (split-plane by default, Hermitian-packed for R2C, interleaved opt-in). A bundled Scheme-like language, Chirp, compiles strings such as (pipeline (rfft :size 4096) (spectral notch) (irfft)) into one fused transform and lets you register your own C callbacks. It is not API-compatible with KissFFT or FFTW: different plan objects, layouts and normalization defaults (NumPy-style unscaled forward).
how_it_is_fast: Transforms are lowered to a 34-opcode IR that either runs on a direct-threaded interpreter (VM) or is emitted as C with AVX2/AVX-512/NEON intrinsics, compiled at runtime by invoking gcc through system(), and dlopen'ed; the AUTO backend switches to the JIT at N >= 128. Version 1.1 added hard-coded split-plane codelets for N = 2-12, recursive split-radix DIF for powers of two >= 16, radix-2/3/4/5 mixed radix for 5-smooth sizes, Rader for primes with 7-smooth N-1, and optional Bluestein. Fused R2C -> pointwise -> C2R pipelines run as one generated kernel.
when_to_use: You want a scriptable or config-driven DSP chain (filter banks, wavelet denoisers, matched filters) where FFT, DWT, CWT and STFT share one API and can be fused, more than raw FFT speed.
Replacing KissFFT on AArch64 for double-precision C2C at N = 8 or N >= 32 (author's run: 16.5 vs 21.7 us at N = 1024, 2238 vs 2735 us at N = 65536, ~1.1-1.8x).
Large power-of-two transforms on x86 AVX2 where the JIT engages (author's Feb 2026 run: 907 vs 3253 us at N = 65536).
Embedding into C projects that can tolerate a runtime C compiler, or builds with FASTANDFOURIER_SINGLE_HEADER=ON to stay VM-only.
when_not_to_use: Raw FFT speed: the README itself says FFTW3 FFTW_MEASURE wins at nearly every size (3-10x ahead on its x86 table), and the same author's Notorious-FFT is 1.2-2.15x faster than FAF on aarch64.
Small and mid sizes on x86: the published x86 table has FAF 2.5-4x slower than KissFFT from N = 64 to 16,384 (e.g. 75.3 vs 27.1 us at N = 1024); it predates the 1.1 codelets and has not been re-run.

Hardened, multi-user or sandboxed processes: the JIT writes generated C and .so files to predictable names in /tmp (faf_jit_<pid>_<counter>), shells out to gcc with system(), and dlopen()s the result and any jit_<hash>.so found in $HOME/.cache/fastandfourier without integrity checks.
Transforms longer than 2^16 points (the VM register file is sized for N <= 65,536) or non-5-smooth lengths without opting into Bluestein (RFFT and DWT refuse it).
Production dependencies needing maturity: 0 stars, no tagged releases on the repo page, and benchmark tables with internal inconsistencies.

integration.dependencies: none at build time beyond libm, libdl and pthread on Linux; a system gcc at runtime for the JIT (otherwise VM only); tests and benchmarks fetch Google Test and Google Benchmark
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.18+, C11 compiler (C++17 only for tests)
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512) and AArch64 (NEON/SVE) on Linux, macOS and Windows per README; CUDA backend experimental
integration.thread_safety: faf_execute_jit_cached is documented thread-safe for concurrent first calls (compare-and-swap pins the kernel to the transform); error messages are thread-local; other guarantees not documented

gotchas: Release builds compile the library with -O3 -march=native -ffast-math -funroll-loops, and the JIT also compiles kernels with -ffast-math and -march=native (or -march=armv8.2-a+fp16 on AArch64 with the SIMD flag), so binaries and cached kernels are not portable to older CPUs and IEEE NaN/Inf semantics are not guaranteed.

The disk cache key is an FNV-1a hash of the IR, size, precision and flags only, not of the library version, compiler or CPU; a stale or foreign jit_<hash>.so in $HOME/.cache/fastandfourier is loaded as-is. faf_jit_destroy also unlinks ctx->so_path, which after a cache hit is the cached file itself, so the cache entry is deleted after it is reused.

The first JIT execution of each transform pays a full gcc invocation; non-power-of-two sizes and kernels that bake process pointers (FFT_STAGE, pipelines) are never disk-cached, so every process recompiles them.

Benchmarks drive the interleaved faf_execute_f64 path, which the README calls the slower convenience path; split-plane buffers are the fast path and require explicit faf_deinterleave/faf_interleave conversion.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: For plain FFTs prefer Notorious-FFT (same author, faster on aarch64), PocketFFT or PFFFT, which beat KissFFT more consistently without a runtime compiler; pick FastAndFourier only when you need its breadth (DCT/DST, DWT, CWT/CQT, STFT, MDCT) behind one API and the Chirp scripting/fusion layer, and can accept the JIT's runtime-compiler and /tmp file model.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Google Benchmark runs, double-precision C2C: on an unnamed 2.3 GHz AVX2 x86_64 Mac (macOS Ventura, -O3 -march=native -ffast-math, 2026-02-22) FAF beat KissFFT only at N = 65,536 (907 vs 3,253 us, about 3.6x) and lost 2.5-4x at N = 64-16,384, with FFTW3 measure fastest everywhere; on an unnamed 6-core 1.73 GHz aarch64 Linux box (-O3 -march=native, frequency scaling on, 2026-09-03) it beat KissFFT by ~1.1-1.8x at N = 8 and N >= 32 and lost slightly at N = 16. Compiler names and CPU models are not stated.
status_note: Actively developed by a single author (last commit 2026-09-25, v1.2.0 commit on 2026-09-04) and MIT-licensed, but young, unstarred and with a security-sensitive JIT design, so treat it as experimental.
